abstraction_design.rationale: The load-bearing abstractions (card, section, speciesCardsFor, the data-driven move tables) stretch across the app's real variation, but the smaller patterns (facts list, count+list section) are copy-pasted and would be copied again for an Items page.

findings.issue: pokemonCard indexes typeLabels with [] but receives a Map from app/src/app.js:72 and a plain object from app/src/app.js:297; the Map lookups silently fail and fall back to humanize.
findings.suggestion: Pick one shape (always a Map, or pre-resolved label strings on each type entry) and pass it consistently from every call site.

findings.issue: A view template imports API_BASE and hardcodes the media URL pattern '/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png', leaking data-source layout into the presentation layer.
findings.suggestion: Resolve sprite URLs in the data layer (api.js) or pass a ready-made spriteUrl prop into pokemonCard.

findings.issue: The 'count + cardList' section markup is copy-pasted three times (lines 32, 38, 77), so any change to list rendering (e.g. adding sort controls) touches each copy.
findings.suggestion: Extract a pokemonListSection(slug, title, count, cards) helper next to section() and reuse it for move/ability/type pages.

findings.issue: The dl.facts pattern is duplicated inline with the Pokémon summary (app/src/views/pokemon.js:33-46); an Items page would copy it a third time.
findings.suggestion: Extract a factsList([{term, description}]) helper into components.js.

findings.issue: PAGE_SIZE, a pagination/data constant, is exported from a view module and consumed by the route (app/src/app.js:66,71).
findings.suggestion: Move PAGE_SIZE into api.js or app.js where the slicing happens.

findings.issue: The client sorter duplicates the server's missing-value token ('—' from app/src/format.js:28); changing one but not the other breaks 'missing sorts last'.
findings.suggestion: Emit the token into the DOM (e.g. data-missing attribute on the table) and read it, or comment both sites pointing at each other.

findings.issue: pokemonMovesData is ~70 lines of data transformation inside the route file, making app.js both router and data munging layer.
findings.suggestion: Move moves data assembly into a src/data/ module (or extend api.js) so app.js stays route+render wiring.

summary: This is a cleanly layered little app: one data module, pure hono/html template functions over plain props, shared card/section abstractions, and an explicit htmx fragment seam, so most changes land in one obvious place. The main editability costs are copy-pasted small patterns (facts dl, count+list markup), a typeLabels parameter that accepts two shapes, and a media-URL pattern leaked into a view template. All are easy fixes; none require restructuring.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Route block (app.js:253-266), import (app.js:28), abilityPage (details.js:35-43), the Pokémon page's Abilities section (pokemon.js:55-64,128) and its data mapping (app.js:194-196). All findable, but three files, and pokemonCard's `hidden` flag becomes dead code unless you also clean components.js.

scenarios.change: Fix the sprite shown for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Every list renders through pokemonCard, whose img src is built at components.js:17 from the id, so one fix covers home, moves, abilities and types. Caveat: cards carry only {id, name}; if the fix needs the Pokémon record's own sprite URL, you must extend speciesIndex (api.js) and speciesCardsFor (app.js), dropping this to 2-3.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Card rendering is shared but ordering lives in two data spots (app.js:65-72, 222-223) and the count+list markup is duplicated three times in details.js, so sort UI and wiring must be added per page. A client-side sort in public/app.js (event-delegated like the table sorter) would touch fewer files but leaves server-rendered order unchanged.
